item.title: White wants Flying Fijians to be braver and more accurate against Italy
item.description: FIJI Water Flying Fijians coach Jake White says while they were pleased with their win last week, the team did not play as well as they should have. White says he expects the players to be more accurate and braver in taking the opportunities they create against Italy this weekend.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Water Flying Fijians coach Jake White says while they were pleased with their win last week, the team did not play as well as they should have.

White says he expects the players to be more accurate and braver in taking the opportunities they create against Italy this weekend.

He says he does not want the players to go into the game without firing a shot.

White says the team has trained really well this week, and the players have been very positive.

White hopes the players can apply what they have learnt over the past eight weeks and hit their straps against Italy on Saturday.

The Flying Fijians play Italy for 11th place at 4.40am Saturday.

item.title: Tailevu names 23-member squad for Farebrother Trophy challenge
item.description: Tailevu has named its 23-member squad, led by captain Eparama Sailo, for Saturday's INKK Farebrother Sullivan Trophy challenge against Nadro at Churchill Park in Lautoka. The match will be played on Saturday, with kick-off scheduled for 3pm.
item.content:encoded:
Tailevu has named its 23-member squad, led by captain Eparama Sailo, for Saturday's INKK Farebrother Sullivan Trophy challenge against Nadro at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

The match will be played on Saturday, with kick-off scheduled for 3pm.

The starting XV will include Lote Tabaki, Manueli Maisamoa, Pio Sovalevu, Kinijoji Taukeisalili and William Devo.

The forwards lineup also features Waisea Niumataiwalu, Avisa Anaqali and Sailo, while Ratu Seru Kaibau has been named at halfback.

The backline includes Kini Douglas, Jope Raderua, William Underwood, Peni Rokoduguni, Josevata Uluinaceva and Maika Selema.

On the bench are Viliame Harehare, Ilaiuia Qasenivalu, Simione Bulai, Malakai Tuikadavu, Emori Logavatu, Pateresio Domodomolagai, Saula Tuinabunawa and Solomone Sautakanavanua.

The match kicks off at 3pm Saturday at Churchill Park, Lautoka.

item.title: Running for mum : Lami's Semanavanua eyes gold at Tuckers Games
item.description: Running for his mother, who travelled all the way from Lami to support him, Setareki Semanavanua has secured his place in the Under-13 400-metres final at this year's Fiji Primary Schools Tuckers Ice Cream Games. Speaking to fijivillage Sports, Semanavanua says he hopes to improve his time in the final and win a gold medal for Lami later today.
item.content:encoded:
Running for his mother, who travelled all the way from Lami to support him, Setareki Semanavanua has secured his place in the Under-13 400-metres final at this year's Fiji Primary Schools Tuckers Ice Cream Games.

Speaking to fijivillage Sports, Semanavanua says he hopes to improve his time in the final and win a gold medal for Lami later today.

The Games are underway at HFC Bank Stadium, with 24 districts taking part in this year's competition.

The heats are currently underway, with young athletes undeterred by the scorching Suva heat as they compete in the hope of bringing glory to their respective districts.

This year's competition has also welcomed the inclusion of new districts, including Wainimala and Koro.

item.title: Young athletes urged to believe in themselves as 2026 Tuckers Games begin
item.description: The Fiji Primary School Athletics Competition will be bringing together young athletes for two days of track and field competition , sportsmanship and school pride. Former Filise and Nadroga Navosa primary school athlete Joana Vakasobuduru is encouraging the young athletes to believe in themselves and never doubt what they can achieve.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Primary School Athletics Competition will be bringing together young athletes for two days of track and field competition , sportsmanship and school pride.

Former Filise and Nadroga Navosa primary school athlete Joana Vakasobuduru is encouraging the young athletes to believe in themselves and never doubt what they can achieve.

Vakasobuduru, who is 21 years old, says her own athletics journey taught her the importance of hard work, discipline and self-belief.

She says growing up, she had the opportunity to represent her school as a runner and long jumper, winning gold medals in different events.

The athlete from Kumi, Verata, Tailevu, with maternal links to Vunibau, Serua, attended Sigatoka Methodist High School, where she competed in long jump and sprint events.

Her sporting talent saw her win a gold medal at the Coca-Cola Games in the Sub-Junior Girls division.

This achievement helped her secure a two-year scholarship to study in the United States at Neosho County Community College in Kansas, where she completed an Associate Degree.

She was later awarded another scholarship to continue her studies at Central Methodist University in Missouri, where she completed her bachelor's degree and graduated.

Vakasobuduru remains in the United States, having successfully combined her sporting talent with academic achievement.

She says athletics will always hold a special place in her heart and is encouraging the young athletes participating in the Tucker Games to make the most of the opportunity.

She urges them to give their best, support one another and wear their Nadroga Navosa colours with pride.

Vakasobuduru says the competition is not just about winning medals but also about making memories, building friendships and enjoying every moment.

She reminds the athletes to dream big, work hard, stay humble and never give up, while making themselves and Nadroga Navosa proud.

item.title: Ikanivere named on the bench as Nasilasila captains Flying Fijians against Italy this Saturday
item.description: Tevita Ikanivere has been named on the bench for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians, with Isoa Nasilasila named captain for their Test against Italy at 4.40am this Saturday. Nasilasila will lead the starting side, which includes Vilikesa Nairai, Peniami Narisia and Inoke Ravuiwasa in the front row, alongside Setareki Turagacoke, Mesake Vocevoce, Elia Canakaivata and Kitione Salawa.
item.content:encoded:
Tevita Ikanivere has been named on the bench for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians, with Isoa Nasilasila named captain for their Test against Italy at 4.40am this Saturday.

Nasilasila will lead the starting side, which includes Vilikesa Nairai, Peniami Narisia and Inoke Ravuiwasa in the front row, alongside Setareki Turagacoke, Mesake Vocevoce, Elia Canakaivata and Kitione Salawa.

Terio Tamani will lead the backline, with Caleb Muntz at fly-half.

They will be joined by Peniasi Dakuwaqa, Vinaya Habosi, Iosefo Masi, Jiuta Wainiqolo and Ponipate Loganimasi.

Ikanivere is among the eight replacements, alongside Luke Tagi, Etonia Waqa, Isikeli Rabitu, Peni Ravai, Joseva Tamani, Frank Lomani and Sireli Maqala.

The Flying Fijians will be looking to put in a strong performance against Italy as they continue their November Test campaign.

Meanwhile, Ireland will be up against Australia at 8.10am on Saturday.

Wales will meet Japan at 1.10am on Sunday, before England takes on New Zealand at 4.40am.

Scotland will face Argentina at 1.10am on Monday, while France and South Africa will battle for the inaugural Nations Championship title at 4.40am.
